title: Zoomed all the way out: which one still has the plants in it?
question: Which of these three reads as crisp, with the plants and the ground both there? Pick one.
context_md:
You reported that zooming all the way out made pixels of plants and other foreground things disappear. They were disappearing: at the widest zoom-out one screen dot has to stand for a 4x4 square of the world, and the view was drawing whichever cell sat at the corner of that square and throwing the other fifteen away. A stem one cell wide had three chances in four of landing in a gap.

Each pane is the same two worlds at the same moment, top the lab bed and bottom the outdoor coast, magnified 2x. **Same world, same seed, same frame in all three** -- only the choosing rule differs.

**The counts under each pane** say how many screen dots actually have a plant or an animal in them, measured by rendering the same world twice and erasing all the life in the second, so it cannot be fooled by colour. *changed* is how many dots differ from the current build: one of these repaints almost the whole screen and two barely touch it.

What I am unsure of and would rather you judged than I argued: whether the busiest option is genuinely better to look at, or just *more*. One pane also softens everything, which I expect you to dislike -- but that is the obvious fix a lot of people would reach for, so it is here to be turned down rather than assumed away.

All three are live behind **shift and the zoom-out key**, so nothing here is a one-way door.
